subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput decision follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput decision follow-up

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Call recap:
- Primary goal: integrate Redwood for real-time payment auth flows and chat-based support.
- Expected traffic profile you mentioned: ~500 qps average, spikes up to ~1.2k qps during batch settlements.
- P95 latency target: ~150ms (hard requirement for auth path); non-auth chat can tolerate up to 300–400ms.

Recommendation (qualification):
- Based on the P95/throughput constraints, Dedicated capacity is the safer default for predictable latency at your scale.
- Hosted API could be used for initial feature work / lower-critical paths while we provision Dedicated capacity.

Next steps I propose:
1) We’ll attach a short latency/throughput worksheet that maps capacity tiers to expected P95s and cost (see attachment).
2) If Dedicated looks right, we’ll draft a short proposal/quote and schedule a procurement call to lock carrier and timeline.
3) If you want, we can run a 2-week pilot on Hosted (no commitment) to validate integrations while Dedicated is being provisioned.

[Attachment: latency-throughput-summary.xlsx]

Can you confirm the qps numbers above and whether Dedicated is what you want us to quote? I can have a draft proposal over to you by EOD Monday if so.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0167
From: Samir Patel <samir@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput decision follow-up

Thanks Marissa — great recap. Confirming the numbers from our end:
- Baseline: 450–550 qps typical (US hours)
- Peak: 1,100–1,300 qps during batch settlement windows (roughly 10–15 minutes, a few times per day)
- P95 target for auth: 150ms or lower; anything higher and we risk increased decline rates.

We’re leaning toward Dedicated for the auth path. We do want to keep the Hosted API as a fallback and for non-critical workloads.

Next for us: procurement needs a quote and an estimated lead time for Dedicated capacity. Can you include an expected SLA and minimum commit terms in the proposal? Also, please include a model for burst handling during peaks.

If you can get a draft proposal by Monday that’d be ideal — procurement meeting is next Thursday.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | FinPay
samir@finpay.com | +1 (212) 555-0179
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 17 Jan 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput decision follow-up

Quick note — agree Dedicated makes the most sense if auth is P95 150ms at 1.2k peak. For sizing, initial recommendation:
- Start with 2x large nodes (8x A100-ish equiv) with autoscale policy to add 1 extra node at 85% CPU/KV-util.
- Enable KV prefix caching for auth paths; it should reduce token overhead.

I’ll draft the tech appendix for the proposal with expected p95 numbers per tier and cost delta between reserved and burst. Will attach to the proposal.

—Neha
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput decision follow-up

Thanks for confirming, Samir — and great, sounds like we’re aligned.

Action items from Redwood:
- I’ll send a draft proposal (Dedicated capacity) + tech appendix from Neha by EOD today. Proposal will include: recommended node sizing, expected P95s by path, SLA language, and pricing for both reserved commit and burst buffer.
- We’ll include a Hosted fallback plan and a 2-week pilot option for non-auth flows if you want to get started earlier.
- Suggested next meeting: procurement + infra on Thu Jan 22 at 10am ET to review quote and timeline. Does that work for you?

Attachments: proposal-dedicated-v1.pdf (draft)

If procurement confirms the go-ahead, we can target Dedicated provisioning within 4–6 business days of signed commitment, subject to quota availability.

Looking forward — I’ll drop the proposal now.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0167
